title: fix(approvals): the console names a position approver `position:NAME`, the spelling the server stores (objectui#11455)
body:
Fixes #11455

Clause-②: no

## What changed

The console now names a position approver the way the server stores it: `position:manager`, not `role:manager`. It sends no `role:` twin as a fallback (triage `5949816132`: "⛔ The console keeps no `role:` fallback").

| Site | What it feeds | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sharedUserFeeds.approverIdentities()` (app-shell) | bell badge, bell Approvals tab, Home To-do (`approverId` query) | `role:manager` per position | `position:manager` per position |
| `approvalsApi.buildApproverIdentities()` (console) | Approvals page "My Pending" filter, Approve / Reject enablement (`identities.some(id => pending.has(id))`), and the `actor_id` a decision sends (`identities.find(i => pending.has(i))`) | `role:manager` per position | `position:manager` per position |

The `sharedUserFeeds` docblock used to say "The `role:` prefix is the SERVER's addressing scheme for `pending_approvers` and stays as it is". It now says what the server stores. Two comments in `ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx` that described the identity scheme with `role:` for a position are corrected too. One changeset covers `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/console`, both as patch.

## Server contract (objectstack `origin/main` `ecb6ca02`, read only)

- **What is stored.** A slot routed to a position nobody held when the request opened keeps the literal `position:NAME`. This is the `type:value` fallback in `resolveApproverSpec` (plugin-approvals `approval-service.ts`).
- **The canonical prefix.** `approver-address.ts` lists `POSITION_ADDRESS_PREFIXES = ['position:', 'role:']`, "canonical first". `role:` is the ADR-0090 D3 deprecated spelling, kept for 15.x-era slots. Per the card, an approve that names `role:NAME` on a `position:NAME` slot answers 403 (objectstack#21379).
- **`user.positions` and `user.role` are different things.** The session's `positions[]` is the server's `grants.positions`, the same set `ExecutionContext.positions` carries and `resolveActor` checks a named address against. plugin-auth's `customSession` says: "⛔ The better-auth `user.role` scalar is NOT a source of it."

## Every `role:` site in objectui, and what happened to it

- **Converted (they name a position):** the two builders above.
- **Kept: `buildApproverIdentities`' scalar arm, `role:` + the better-auth `user.role`.** This is not a position (see `customSession` above). Renaming it to `position:` would claim a position the session never reported. The brief says "don't touch a genuine role identity that is not a position", so it is unchanged and pinned as the control.
- **Kept: display formatters that read stored values.** These are `formatIdentity` in `packages/app-shell/src/utils/approverIdentity.ts`, its copy in `ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx`, and the comment in `approvalOverride.ts`. They label `role:` entries that the server still stores for 15.x-era slots. They build no identity and send nothing.
- **Kept: tests and fixtures of stored values.** `approverIdentity.test.ts` checks `formatIdentity('role:admin')`, and `approvalOverride.test.ts` has a `pending_approvers` fixture with `role:sales_manager`. Both describe stored slots, not what the console sends.
- **Converted with the builders:** the pins in `sharedUserFeeds.approverPositions.test.tsx` and `approvalsApi.approverIdentities.test.ts`.
- No other decide path exists. `useRecordApprovals` decides nothing (objectui#3055) and gates on the server's `viewer` block.

## Tests (at `13282bf60`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over 36 files, run from the worktree root through `os-verify-lock.sh`. The set is every app-shell test that names `sharedUserFeeds`, `approverIdentities`, `pending_approvers` or a quoted `role:` prefix, plus every console test that names `buildApproverIdentities`, `approvalsApi` or `ApprovalsInboxPage`. Result: `Test Files  36 passed (36)`, `Tests  333 passed (333)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` passes (exit 0). It runs `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and `--listFiles` shows it includes `sharedUserFeeds.approverPositions.test.tsx`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check` passes (exit 0). `--listFiles` shows it includes all three console files this PR changes, the test among them.
- Both type-checks ran after building the dependency closure (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/console^...'`, which contains app-shell).

**Pins.** For each builder:
- the position-addressed subset is exactly `position:NAME` for every session position;
- no `role:` entry names a position.

The app-shell list has no `role:` entry at all. The console list keeps only the scalar's `role:user`.

**Controls that must not move.** id and email in both builders, and the console's scalar `role:auditor` / comma-split cases.

**The docblock.** Its sentence was checked by reading it, not by a test. Prose is not pinned.

## Reverse verification (prediction written before running)

- **BASE leg.** The `4a1adb76e` source of both builders was run against the new pins. Predicted 1 + 3 red. Result: `Tests  4 failed | 10 passed (14)`.
  - app-shell: `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'position:manager', …(1) ]`.
  - console: case 1, the repeated-position case and the two-sources case went red (`expected [ 'u_1', 'role:user', 'role:manager' ] to deeply equal [ 'u_1', 'position:user', …(2) ]`).
  - Every control stayed green.
  - Restore: `git checkout HEAD --` on absolute paths. The blob hashes match HEAD (`80afdffebfad`, `83ccddd39df8`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Ablation leg.** `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (objectstack) put the `role:` prefix back on each position arm. In each case the anchor went 1 to 0 and the blob changed.
  - app-shell: `Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)`.
  - console: `Tests  3 failed | 6 passed (9)`.
  - Each restore was proven: blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
  - The direction was as predicted. The scalar-role and id/email controls stayed green.

## Gates

All exit 0:
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `0 new citation(s)`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: `5 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims`: it asks for one re-read, of `.changeset/6730-shared-activity-type-bucket.md`. That paragraph is about `mapActivityRows`, which this PR does not touch, so it is still true.
- `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`
- `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 6 paths: `NOT GOVERNED`.

**ESLint, narrowed to the 5 changed source files.** Three facts make this narrowed run count as a measurement:
- **Population.** It comes from ESLint's own config. `ESLint#isPathIgnored` answers false for all 5, and `calculateConfigForFile` resolves 116 to 119 rules for each.
- **Count.** It comes from `--format json`: 5 files linted, 0 errors, 20 warnings. BASE has the same 20 warnings (19 + 1, read through `--stdin` from `4a1adb76e`).
- **Untouched files are unaffected.** Type-aware linting is off: `parserOptions.project` and `projectService` are unset for every changed file. No rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem. So this diff cannot change ESLint's result for any file it did not touch.

The repo-wide `pnpm lint` run is left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **Legacy `role:` slots.** A 15.x-era slot still stored as `role:manager` stays listed (the server folds both spellings, objectstack PR #21378). But it no longer enables Approve / Reject on the Approvals page through the position alone. The page decides that with a literal client-side comparison against `pending_approvers`. This follows from the ruled "no `role:` fallback" and is stated in the changeset. Not filed.
- **The scalar arm can enable a button the server would refuse.** The server reads `role:` only as a position spelling and lets a caller act under it only for a position they hold. `sys_user.role` is not projected into positions. So on a literal `role:` slot whose name equals the scalar, the console can enable Approve and the server would answer 403. This is an inference from reading the code, not reproduced. Not filed. Carrier: none.
- **Display gap.** The local `formatIdentity` copy in `ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx` has no `position:` branch, so `position:sales_manager` shows truncated. app-shell's copy prettifies it through the directory binding. Display polish, not filed. Carrier: none.
- **Claim surface.** The claim (`5951880439`) declares an app-shell file surface. The two `apps/console` files were converted because the dispatch order said to convert every objectui site that names a position with `role:`, and `buildApproverIdentities` is the decide path the card's 403 is about. The seat may want to widen the claim's surface to match.

The session of record is `https://claude.ai/code/session_01YLg8XqWGJ785fwQ5v4pH37`.
